A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Robust Decision Transformer work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, revised, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original offline RL experiments on MuJoCo, Kitchen, and Adroit, including corruption benchmarks, ablations, and test-time perturbation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds experiments on NeoRL, transformer-backed baselines, dataset sensitivity, and correction mechanisms.

M1.justification: The proposed RDT retains embedding dropout, Gaussian-weighted action/reward losses, and iterative action/reward correction. Algorithm 1 is functionally unchanged. v2 corrects v1's inconsistent prose about correcting states; v1's algorithm and implementation already specified action/reward correction.

E1.justification: v2 adds NeoRL CityLearn and Finance, MuJoCo medium-v2 and expert-v2 data, mixed adversarial corruption, and mixed-corruption training combined with test-time perturbations. Original benchmark coverage remains, including full-data MuJoCo results relocated to Appendix D.6.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator set is retained. Section 4.5 and Figure 7 add UWMSG and RIQL variants with transformer policy backbones, substantially extending comparisons that control for architecture. v2 Figure 6 also adds vanilla DT to the main component ablation.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes reported hyperparameters: MuJoCo (10%) Gaussian coefficients increase from (0.1, 0.1) to (1.0, 1.0), and Kitchen coefficients from (10, 10) to (30, 30), alongside dropout and correction-threshold changes. New protocols include dataset-size sweeps, 2% quality-level subsets, and transformer-backbone controls. NeoRL sampling fractions remain ambiguous because Appendix D.12 and Table 10 disagree.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing ablations, v2 adds dropout-strategy comparisons, clean/corrupted-loss and correction-error diagnostics, transformer-backbone controls, leave-one-component-out ablations, dataset-size sensitivity, RIQL convergence curves, detection precision, and state-prediction/correction failure tests. These address substantial additional questions about mechanisms and robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions already report four-seed experiments, uncertainty values, and error bars. v2 Section 4.1 newly describes the across-seed dispersion as 'standard variance,' providing a limited reporting clarification with imprecise terminology. No increase in run count or new significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Numerous existing scores change, and new benchmarks and diagnostics add results. For example, RDT's random-action halfcheetah (10%) score changes from 13.8±2.3 in v1 Table 5 to 20.4±1.7 in v2 Table 1. Because corresponding hyperparameters change, this is a revised result rather than an established same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Section 2 changes the RL objective from an infinite discounted horizon with gamma in [0,1) to a finite T-step horizon allowing gamma=1. This is a limited formal specification revision. RDT's mathematical rules remain equivalent, and neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v2's Introduction explicitly presents construction of a challenging limited-data benchmark as a contribution, whereas v1 primarily presents these datasets as evaluation settings. The central claims about sequence-model robustness, the three-component RDT, and combined training/testing robustness remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations concerning information loss from raw-input masking, correction reliability during training, and the differing effects of transformer backbones on RIQL and UWMSG. Appendix D.6 acknowledges possible RIQL undertraining on full datasets. Appendix D.14 and Section E expand the state-prediction limitation with dynamics-learning and prediction-error explanations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code link, explicit dataset-access links, and a reproducibility statement. New Appendix C.4 supplies per-task trajectory and transition counts instead of v1's approximate size description. Hyperparameter disclosures are revised, although full-data MuJoCo settings disappear from Table 3. Additional experiments document subset fractions and baseline architecture modifications.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly connects RDT to supervised noisy-label learning and dropout through added references including Song, Chang, Reed, and Gal and Ghahramani. It also adds selected masking, non-stationarity, transformer-RL, and NeoRL references, while removing the Furuta citation. The principal positioning against temporal-difference approaches remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, Introduction, and method explanations undergo substantial rewriting. The experimental narrative is reordered, with corruption-strength analysis moved to Appendix D.4 and observation-perturbation evaluation brought forward. v2 also changes the title and author information and adds contents, ethics, reproducibility, and limitations sections.

P2.justification: The main random-corruption table changes from task-group averages to detailed per-task results, while full-data MuJoCo results receive a separate appendix table. Other tables are reorganized by attack type. Mixed-corruption plots gain an adversarial panel, numerous diagnostic displays are added, existing figures are relocated or redrawn, and the document adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical substantiation through architecture-controlled comparisons, direct validation of weighting and correction, and documented failure cases, addressing important attribution and mechanism gaps in v1. Broader domain evaluation and improved implementation access and dataset documentation add further value. New reporting defects remain, including conflicting NeoRL sampling fractions and a Finance improvement percentage inconsistent with Table 10, but these localized problems do not outweigh the substantial gains.
